result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings (including the shared rules in the module docstring) and fixed them all. After the fix, all 150 rules match their docstrings in the check described below.

| Rule | What was wrong | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 17, 44, 50 | The discount was rounded with `round()`, but the common rule says to round down to the won. | Changed to `// 100` |
| 43 | The discount started at 21 units instead of 20. | `qty >= 20` |
| 56 | The discount started at 51 units instead of 50. | `qty >= 50` |
| 46, 57 | The cap was applied to the price amount instead of the discount. | Calculate the discount first, then cap it with `min(disc, cap)` |
| 49, 134 | The cap only applied when the discount was over 60,000 won. | Always apply `min(disc, 30000)` |
| 61 | The rate was 13% instead of 12%. | 12% |
| 74 | The rate was 8% instead of 7%. | 7% |
| 127 | The rate was 3% instead of 2%. | 2% |

**How I checked:** I wrote a script that reads each rule's type, rate, minimum quantity and cap from its docstring and builds a reference calculation. It compares every rule against that reference for quantities from 0 to 129 (plus a few large values) and a range of unit prices. Before the fix, it flagged exactly the 12 rules above; after the fix, none fail.

One rule 127 change was applied by a find-and-replace that also matched rule 133, which has identical code. The check caught it, and I restored rule 133 to 3%.

STATUS: DONE
